note: A screen, not an audit: questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them. No savings are computed; typical benefits are the cited sources' general wording.

questions.question: Is cooling tower blowdown manual, with no conductivity control or makeup and blowdown metering?

evidence.text: equipment DRY reads "DRY Fictional cooling tower dry cooler"
no conductivity element or controller near the tower

where: a walkdown: conductivity of makeup and tower water

questions.decision_rule: Raise cycles with a conductivity controller where the water chemistry allows.

typical_benefit.wording: "Increasing cycles from three to six reduces cooling tower make-up water by 20% and cooling tower blowdown by 50%." Recommends a conductivity controller and makeup/blowdown flow meters. No energy % stated.
typical_benefit.arc: 2.2611 (IAC/ITAC browse page: 55 recommendations, 0.9 yr average payback, 45.7% implemented; average dollar figure omitted)
source_titles: S21: DOE FEMP, Best Management Practice #10: Cooling Tower Management
S24: DOE IAC/ITAC database: browse pages, download, schema document

questions.limits: IAC/ITAC figures are browse-page averages read through a summarizing fetch and not re-verified against the downloadable database; averages are skewed by outliers.
